key_insight: Manually curated EHR features plus NLP produced the best acute pancreatitis identification, while a simpler automated model nearly matched it when trained on maximum lipase values.
clinical_relevance: For phenotyping in health systems, clinically informed automation can substantially reduce manual effort without major loss in accuracy.
method: Compared a custom ML approach using manually curated structured claims data with an automated feature-engineering approach.
Trained custom models on validated outcomes from medical record review; automated models used low-cost silver-standard outcomes.
Tested whether adding NLP-derived covariates or using maximum lipase as the training outcome improved performance.
evidence_signal: In evaluation, the custom model reached cv-AUC 0.89-0.91, the automated diagnosis-code model 0.80, and the automated maximum-lipase model 0.88; at 90% PPV, sensitivities were 92%, 45%, and 84%, respectively.
watch_item: The automated approach depended on phenotype-specific knowledge (maximum lipase), so performance may not generalize to outcomes without similarly informative proxy measures.
paper_title: A Comparison of Manual and Automated Approaches to Developing Computable Algorithms for Identifying Acute Pancreatitis
